text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
AL-AHRAM

- President Hosni Mubarak and Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan had talks on bilateral cooperation in all domains, especially industrial cooperation, joint ventures and increasing the volume of trade between Egypt and Turkey. They also dealt with Turkey's political relations with Arab and Islamic countries, including Syria.

- Defence Minister Mohamed Hussein Tantawi, in interview with al-Ahram, says Israel's claim that nuclear wepaons ensure its security is of doubtful validity. The purpose of the Badr 96 manoeuvres was to deter possible attack from any quarter. The Damascus Declaration still exists and is a sound and effective foundation when all its stages are completed.
- Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat arrives in Cairo tomorrow to brief Mubarak on the Washington summit. He will make lightning visits to Italy and France before coming to Egypt.

- Mubarak, in phone conversation with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, told him that there must be movement in the framework of the agreements and commitments already signed between Israel and the Palestinians, as well as urgent measures to ease the closure imposed on the self-rule territories.
- New book says Queen Elizabeth opposed Sir Anthony Eden's plans to attack Egypt in the Suez crisis.
AL-AKHBAR
- Erbakan says the Washington summit did not achieve the results desired. Opening the tunnel under holy sites in Jerusalem is unacceptable to the Islamic world.
- An Arab diplomatic source in Damascus that Arab states are agreed that straight after the U.S. elections they will hold a summit in Damascus, including Iraq.
- Under a presidential decree, 2,500 prisoners will be released on Sunday morning to mark celebrations of the Glorious October Victory (in the Middle East war of 1973).
- A front-page editorial by Galal Duweidar says the Washington summit foundered on the rock of the obstinacy and arrogance of Netanyahu and his hostility to peace.
AL-GOMHURIA

- The next few hours will see urgent contacts between Arab leaders to deal with the situation after the failure of the Washington summit. Arab diplomatic sources in Cairo expect these will lead to an Arab summit or at least Arab meetings at summit level. Political observers doubt that disputes will be settled at the meeting on Sunday at the Erez crossing.
- Supply and Trade Minister Ahmed Gueily says the IMF board will approve Egypt's structural reform programme and the waiver of the third tranche of debt, about $4 billion.

- Ibrahim Fawzi, head of the General Authority for Investment, said 95 percent of the articles in the partnership agreement with the European Union have been finished and negotiations are under way on the remaining five percent.
AL-WAFD
- U.S. State Department critical of Mubarak's decision to miss the summit. "It would have been much better if President Mubarak had come to Washington," spokesman says.
AL-SHAAB
- Columnist Adel Hussein says: "The so-called peace is finished and we will have to fight. Let's be ready."
- Mass demonstrations in universities in protest at the Israeli violations.
- Washington summit is abject failure.
